name: Andy Jassy

career.title: Marketing manager; ran early marketing team and later the compact disc business
Founding leader of AWS (launched 2006 with a 57-person team)

background_rationale: Joined Amazon as a marketing manager straight out of business school and built his career running internal businesses, most notably founding and leading Amazon Web Services for 18 years before becoming CEO.

notable.summary: Told corporate employees they would be required to work in the office five days a week starting January 2025.
In a memo to employees, said generative AI would reduce Amazon's total corporate workforce over the next few years as efficiency gains take hold.
Amazon cut about 16,000 corporate jobs, following roughly 14,000 cuts in October 2025, describing the moves as reducing layers and bureaucracy.
In his annual shareholder letter, defended plans for about $200 billion in 2026 capital spending, mostly on AI infrastructure, writing that Amazon was not investing it "on a hunch."

personal_story.hook: Andy Jassy wanted to be a sportscaster; instead he joined Amazon in 1997 and went on to build AWS.
personal_story.summary: Jassy grew up in Scarsdale, New York, a Giants fan who played varsity soccer and tennis and dreamed of becoming a professional athlete. After graduating from Harvard College in 1990, he tried sportscasting, sports production, coaching and paralegal work, worked as a project manager at collectibles company MBI, and co-founded a small company that he later shut down. He started at Amazon in 1997 the Monday after his last Harvard Business School exam, without knowing what his job or title would be. As Jeff Bezos's technical adviser, or 'shadow,' he helped develop the idea that became Amazon Web Services, which he ran for years before succeeding Bezos as CEO in 2021.
